_comment: Octail curated egg (plan §6.4). Based on games-steamcmd stormworks/egg-pterodactyl-stormworks--build-and-rescue.json (pelican-eggs, MIT licence) at 8dd208975977aa24a6c53008a65a630c150806b8, which downloaded the free Stormworks Dedicated Server tool (app 1247090) anonymously. Geometa turned that app into a stub (its server64.exe only prints "The Stormworks dedicated server has been moved!"): the server now ships with the base game, app 573090, which SteamCMD only downloads for an account that owns Stormworks. So the egg uses Octail's steam_login feature (required): the Steam account picked on the Startup tab logs in, Steam Guard codes are asked for in the console and the login is cached for start-time updates (the wine image's SteamCMD hook logs in with it). The install refuses anonymous logins, downloads the Windows depot of app 573090 and fails when server64.exe or rom/ is missing. Upstream configured nothing (its README: edit server_config.xml by hand, port included). Octail writes a first server_data/server_config.xml in the install (the mission playlists from the installed rom/data/missions) and sets the port, name, password, max players and save name in it with sed before every start, whatever the layout the server wrote it back in (Octail has no xml parser), removes Wine's 32-bit cmd.exe before every start (the server clears its console through it every few seconds, which stutters clients), starts with the image's Xvfb instead of xvfb-run, detects the start from 'Server Version : v...' or the bound game port (x_octail.features.ready), reserves the two ports the server opens after the game port (Steam query +1 and +2, fixed_ports), adds the stormworks tag, the no_console_input flag, install sandbox defaults and resource hints, stops with Ctrl+C handed to the server by a trap (the wine image runs the line in bash as PID 1, which ignores it otherwise) and waits for it so the config and world are saved, turns Auto Update on (upstream: off and hidden), refuses " < > & \ ~ in the name and password (they go into XML through sed). SteamCMD is retried up to 3 times: its first run on a fresh install often fails with "Missing configuration". SteamCMD exits 0 even when an install failed (Missing configuration), so its retry loop counts a run as done only on SteamCMD's "Success! App" line.
name: Stormworks: Build and Rescue
author: iamkubi@gmail.com
description: Design, build and pilot your own air-sea rescue service. The Windows dedicated server from the base game, run under Wine; needs a Steam account that owns Stormworks.

startup_commands.Default: export SteamAppId=573090; rm -f "${WINEPREFIX:-/home/container/.wine}/drive_c/windows/syswow64/cmd.exe"; CFG=server_data/server_config.xml; sw_set() { sed -i -E "s~(^|[[:space:]])$1=\"[^\"]*\"~\1$1=\"$2\"~" "${CFG}"; }; if [ -f "${CFG}" ]; then sw_set port "{{SERVER_PORT}}"; sw_set name "{{SERVER_NAME}}"; sw_set password "{{SERVER_PASSWORD}}"; sw_set max_players "{{MAX_PLAYERS}}"; sw_set save_name "{{SAVE_NAME}}"; else echo "Octail: ${CFG} is missing; reinstall the server to get it back."; fi; wine ./server64.exe +server_dir server_data & SW_PID=$!; trap "kill -INT ${SW_PID} 2>/dev/null; wait ${SW_PID}" INT TERM; wait ${SW_PID}

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Stormworks: Build and Rescue dedicated server, the Windows build (it runs under Wine).
# The free Stormworks Dedicated Server tool (app 1247090) is now a stub: the server ships with the base game, app 573090,
# which SteamCMD only downloads for a Steam account that owns Stormworks.
# Octail's steam_login feature fills STEAM_USER and, for this install only, STEAM_PASS; Steam Guard codes are asked
# for in the console.
## Server Files: /mnt/server
set -uo pipefail

if [ -z "${STEAM_USER:-}" ] || [ "${STEAM_USER}" = anonymous ]; then
    echo "The Stormworks server can't be downloaded anonymously: it ships with the game, so pick a Steam account that"
    echo "owns Stormworks on the Startup tab (Steam account), then reinstall the server."
    exit 1
fi
echo "Logging in to Steam as ${STEAM_USER}"

## download and install steamcmd
cd /tmp || exit 1
mkdir -p /mnt/server/steamcmd
curl -fsSL -o steamcmd.tar.gz https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/client/installer/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz || { echo "Downloading SteamCMD failed."; exit 1; }
tar -xzf steamcmd.tar.gz -C /mnt/server/steamcmd || exit 1
mkdir -p /mnt/server/steamapps # Fix steamcmd disk write error when this folder is missing
## Octail: servers installed from the old app 1247090 (now a stub) drop its manifest; app 573090 replaces its files
rm -f /mnt/server/steamapps/appmanifest_1247090.acf

## the account's saved login (Tentacle's login cache), so later updates log in without the password
if [ -n "${STEAM_LOGIN_CACHE:-}" ]; then
    rm -rf /mnt/server/steamcmd/config && ln -s "${STEAM_LOGIN_CACHE}" /mnt/server/steamcmd/config
fi
cd /mnt/server/steamcmd || exit 1

# SteamCMD fails otherwise for some reason, even running as root.
chown -R root:root /mnt/server/steamcmd /mnt/server/steamapps
export HOME=/mnt/server

LOGIN=("${STEAM_USER}")
[ -n "${STEAM_PASS:-}" ] && LOGIN+=("${STEAM_PASS}")
[ -n "${STEAM_AUTH:-}" ] && LOGIN+=("${STEAM_AUTH}")

## install the game with steamcmd (the Windows depot: the server runs under Wine)
## Octail: SteamCMD's first run often fails with "Missing configuration"; try up to 3 times
for steamcmd_try in 1 2 3; do
    if ./steamcmd.sh +force_install_dir /mnt/server $( [[ "${WINDOWS_INSTALL}" == "1" ]] && printf %s '+@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType windows' ) +login "${LOGIN[@]}" +app_update "${SRCDS_APPID}" validate +quit 2>&1 | tee /tmp/steamcmd.log && grep -q "Success! App '" /tmp/steamcmd.log && ! grep -q "ERROR! Failed to install app" /tmp/steamcmd.log; then break; fi
    echo "SteamCMD did not finish (attempt $steamcmd_try of 3)"
done

## set up 32 and 64 bit Steam client libraries
mkdir -p /mnt/server/.steam/sdk32 /mnt/server/.steam/sdk64
cp -v linux32/steamclient.so /mnt/server/.steam/sdk32/steamclient.so
cp -v linux64/steamclient.so /mnt/server/.steam/sdk64/steamclient.so

## Octail: fail the install when SteamCMD didn't download the server
## (rom/ too: the old app 1247090 stub also had a server64.exe, the base game has the game data next to it)
if [[ ! -f "/mnt/server/server64.exe" ]] || [[ ! -d "/mnt/server/rom" ]]; then
    echo -e "\nSteamCMD failed to install Stormworks. The Steam account must own Stormworks;"
    echo "check the login lines above, then reinstall."
    exit 1
fi

## Octail: the server reads server_data/server_config.xml (+server_dir server_data) and writes it back when it stops.
## A first config with the mission playlists the installed game ships, so the server's port is right from the first
## start; Octail sets the port, name, password, max players and save name in it before every start.
mkdir -p /mnt/server/server_data
CFG=/mnt/server/server_data/server_config.xml
if [[ ! -f "$CFG" ]]; then
    {
        echo '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>'
        echo '<server_data port="25564" name="Octail Stormworks Server" save_name="autosave_server" max_players="16" password="">'
        printf '\t<admins>\n\t</admins>\n\t<authorized>\n\t</authorized>\n\t<blacklist>\n\t</blacklist>\n\t<whitelist>\n\t</whitelist>\n'
        if [[ -d /mnt/server/rom/data/missions ]]; then
            printf '\t<playlists>\n'
            for mission in /mnt/server/rom/data/missions/*/; do
                printf '\t\t<path path="rom/data/missions/%s"/>\n' "$(basename "$mission")"
            done
            printf '\t</playlists>\n'
        fi
        echo '</server_data>'
    } > "$CFG"
fi

## install end
echo "-----------------------------------------"
echo "Installation completed..."
echo "-----------------------------------------"

variables.name: Server Name
variables.description: The name in the server list (no " < > & \ or ~). Written to server_config.xml.

variables.name: Server Password
variables.description: Optional: players must enter it to join. Empty = no password (no " < > & \ or ~).

variables.name: Max Players
variables.description: How many players may join at once.

variables.name: Save Name
variables.description: The world save (server_data/saves/<name>). A new name starts a new world; the old one stays.

variables.name: Auto Update
variables.description: Update the server with SteamCMD (the saved login of the server's Steam account) before every start (1 = on, 0 = off).

variables.name: Steam App ID
variables.description: The SteamCMD app: the base game, which carries the dedicated server (the old server tool, 1247090, is a stub).

variables.name: Windows Install
variables.description: Downloads the Windows build (the server runs under Wine).
